posts.name: MindWanderer
posts.cooked:
Also, FYI, Madame Mittermeier's isn't showing up on the randomizer, because it's hard-coded (to include expansion data) and it's misspelled in the Google form.

Out of curiosity, since we have all the normal villains we're ever going to have now, I took a look at where the difficulty levels stand.  Looking for obvious breaks, the difficulty levels seem to be about this:

Difficulty 1:

  • Tormented Infinitor
  • Unstable Kismet
  • Chokepoint
  • Ambuscade
  • Gloomweaver
  • Deadline

Difficulty 2:

  • The Ennead
  • Baron Blade
  • Apostate
  • Kismet
  • Mad Bomber Blade
  • Wager Master

Borderline difficulty 2/3:

  • Akash'bhuta
  • Miss Information

Difficulty 3:

  • Spite
  • Omnitron
  • Grand Warlord Voss
  • Plague Rat
  • Citizen Dawn

Borderline difficulty 3/4:

  • Skinwalker Gloomweaver
  • Progeny
  • Infinitor
  • La Capitan

Difficulty 4:

  • The Matriarch
  • Agent of Gloom Spite
  • The Dreamer
  • The Chairman
  • Cosmic Omnitron
  • Vengeance Style (on average)

Difficulty 5:

  • Iron Legacy
  • Kaargra Warfang

Iron Legacy and Kaarga really do deserve a category of their own.  The gap between them and everyone else is tremendous.  It's interesting to see where >G got the difficulties right, and where they got them completely wrong.  The promos are largely way off, but not as badly as Deadline, Gloomweaver, and Omnitron.

posts.name: MindWanderer
posts.cooked:
New statistics added to the report: 

On the Heroes page, probability of each hero being incapacitated, and probability of going on to win given that the hero was incapacitated.

On the Villains page, probability that the villain will flip at least once during the game, and probability that the heroes will win given a game in which the hero does or does not flip.

On the Details page of each villain, the count of the number of times games ended in different ways.  Since we're on the topic of Kaargra: only 26% of Normal Kaargra's wins are due to hero incapacitation, and 17% of Advanced Kaargra's.

This is also the point at which error on the part of the contributors becomes extremely apparent.  For instance, a substantial number of people reported beating Baron Blade, Miss Information, The Dreamer, The Chairman, and Skinwalker Gloomweaver without flipping them.  However, the overall trends seem credible.

I realize I totally dropped the ball on getting you proper data. However I have picked the ball back up!

Attached you can find one week of data (2017-02-01 to 2017-02-08) from Google Analytics, representative of everything we're looking to share so far.

There are 3 platforms: Desktop (Steam), iOS, and Android.

There are 4 events: Game Start, Game Start (Team Mode), Game End, and Game End (Team Mode).

Each file includes the info about its context at the top, then a series of rows. Each row has a "dimension1" with JSON describing the game setup (and result for Game End events), and total_events which can be more than 1 if more than 1 player started or ended the same setup (esp common for the weekly one-shot setups).

Note that the Team Mode records are formatted differently than classic mode; this is due to some restrictions we have on the # of parameters we are allowed to record in some systems.

You will also see some challenge mode parameters; it turns out the data from beta testers is mixed in, which is a bit odd but shouldn't really be a problem I think.

It's up to you if you want to infer anything from the difference between Game Start and Game End events; note that the data doesn't tie anything between a particular user, so there will be some oddness in the data around report boundaries if you do so.

The file format can be changed; right now it's just dumping out the data from Google Analytics in Python. Please let me know if there's any simple transformation I can do that might help if you're having trouble importing it.

Once you're happy with the data format and interpretation and all that, I can generate all the historical data. And then we can coordinate on a schedule for data dumps and how to get them to you on an ongoing basis.

SotM Report 2017-02-01 to 2017-02-08.zip (245 KB)

posts.name: MigrantP
posts.cooked: One thing to watch out for when interpreting the data is that a multiplayer game will have the same events recorded for each player. For example, if me and two friends play a game, the total_events for that game will be incremented by 3 from our single game. It may make sense for a first stab to ignore any events with total_events > 1, or treat them specially.

All right, I have some sample pages with the data I have so far: 

http://mindwanderer.net/sotm/app-stats-full.html

That's just using the week's worth of data I got, and for simplicity it's only the desktop data, and only standard games (not Vengeance).  I'd like to have the file format finalized before I set it up to handle a whole array of input files instead of just one.  It also only counts completed games, as I'd have to figure out a whole separate way of handling abandoned games, and, as we discussed earlier, it treats multiple copies of the exact same setup and result as a single game (to handle multiplayer, and it also helps balance out weekly one-shots being overweighted).  Obviously, all the names of things aren't in their human-friendly format, as I'll have to manually map the "code" names to the common names.

grysqrl:

Dandolo wrote:

Am I the only one who finds comparing datasets fun?
We should set up a series of polls to find out.

LOL!

Anyway, yes, my plan was to keep them separate.

First of all, there's data in the custom form that Handelabra doesn't collect, such as whether villains flipped or heroes were incapacitated.

Second, the app is likely to be skewed, for instance, there's a lot of abandoned games, and there's no way of knowing why they were abandoned (a forfeit would count as a loss, but an "oops, I set this up wrong" or a "there's a new one-shot, I'd rather play that instead" wouldn't.

And third, the app will of course, for at least another year or so, be behind the physical game in terms of what content is available–and that's ignoring Sentinels of Earth Prime, which, if lynkfox agrees, I would also like to add to the stats project but which will probably never make it into the app.
